newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end up as selective blue chips in demand.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end up as selective blue chips in demand.

text.p: Demand in selective blue chips boosted the index to a firm close, but dealers and analysts said the market's recent woes may not be over yet.
The key Composite Index gained 17.23 points to 1.65 percent to end at 1,058.62 on Tuesday.
They said Malaysian funds chased up prices of cheapened large-capitalised stocks but these may face pressure through the week by investors not convinced that the market has stabilised.
"Local funds and state-owned funds were buying but they were specific in which ones to collect," said an institutional dealer at a local brokerage house.
"We have broken 1,050 and are now looking at 1,080. But there's no fast run-up," he added.

Participants said there was still caution in case the U.S. boosts its interest rates after Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee. "If the U.S. do not raise rates, it could be worse because the uncertainty will still be there," said a Vickers Ballas analyst. Malaysian markets are closed on Wednesday for the Buddhist observance of Wesak Day.
Among key blue chip gainers were financial stocks Maybank, Commerce Asset, DCB Holdings and AMMB, up between 15 and 70 cents.
